findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

1) The blade of the can opener in the kitchen was observed heavily soiled. The PIC believed that the equipment was used last the day before observation. 2) The nozzle for the soda gun at the bar farthest from the door was observed heavily soiled around the inside of the nozzle. Both items were shown to staff and washed during the inspection to correct the violations.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY (TCS) FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

1) Rice and cooked macaroni were observed with internal temperatures of 54F-65F during the inspection in the top of a prep cooler. The PIC was shown and discarded the items to correct. Investigation showed the cooler had been shut off on accident. The cooler was switched back on and the foods discarded to correct. 2) TCS foods in the cooler under the grills were observed with internal temperatures of 45F-56F. The PIC was shown and discarded the TCS foods in the cooler to correct the immediate concern. Foods discarded include fish, chicken. Beef patties, cheeses and grilled onions. This corrects the immediate violation for this situation. Refer to line item #33 for a scheduled follow-up for the cooler.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. 

The cooler located under the grill was observed to not be holding TCS foods at correct temperature. The PIC called for maintinance to be conducted during the inspection. A follow-up was set for 10 days to ensure that the cooler is brought into compliance.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.citation_text:
3-305.14 Food Preparation. During preparation, unPACKAGED FOOD shall be protected from environmental sources of contamination. 

A charger cord was observed hanging down from a shelf and laying partially on the counter beneath. This counter has food preparation take place on it. The PIC was shown and instructed to ensure that the cord does not hang down moving forward. Ensure that foods are protected form contamination at all times. The cord was moved to correct.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. 

A half gallon of half n’ half is observed with an internal temperature of approximately 47F. The air temperature in this cooler was between 47F-49F. The front of house manager was consulted and discarded the dairy product to correct the immediate violation. The plan is to use any of the other coolers in this area moving forward as they were all observed at acceptable temperatures.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114.

Multiple moist rags were observed throughout the facility on counters or shelves. These items should have been held between uses in the nearby sani buckets to prevent pathogenic growth. The PIC was shown and the situation discussed. Ensure that all in use rags are stored between uses in buckets of sufficient sanitizer concentration to prevent pathogen growth. The rags were moved during the inspection to their buckets to correct.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed no hand soap to be present at bar hand sink. Discussed with PIC, soap was refilled. Ensure soap is present at all hand sink to ensure proper hand washing is practiced.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed multiple TCS items to be kept past 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, items were pulled and discarded. Ensure any TCS item is kept no longer than 7 days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed no paper towels to be present at the bar hand sink. Discussed with PIC, paper towels were brought to hand sink. Ensure all hand washing stations are properly equipped with soap and paper towels.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed TCS items in an ice bath cold holding at 50F. Discussed with PIC, there was no water in the ice bath. Water was added to the ice bath, and TCS items were observed to be at 40F. Ensure staff is properly preparing ice baths to ensure TCS foods kept in it can be properly cold held at or below 41F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.comment:

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: Observed sanitizer bucket in kitchen to test at 0ppm (Quat). Discussed with PIC, buckets were remade and tested at 200 ppm. Ensure facility has a sanitizer bucket available at the proper concentration during all hours of operation.

findings.comment:

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

A Certified Food Protection Manager is not available at the facility at the time of this inspection. Hand outs were given for the local courses known by this department. The facility is instructed to ensure that there are enough CFPMs available so as to cover all times that food handling practices are taking place in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

The quat sanitizer in the bar three part sink is observed between 0-100 ppm on both the inspector and facility test strips. The bartender indicated that they had changed the water at the start of their shift approximately half an hour before observation. The bottle of tablets used for this solution was read and the bartender notified that 1-2 tablets are required PER GALLON OF WATER to reach an effective concentration of 200-400 ppm in solution. More tablets were added to the solution to produce the correct concentration. bartenders shouls check the concentration when made to ensure that it is at effective levels.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below). 

A container (not the original) of pink soap is on the shelf above the three part sink and appears to have gone bad. A grainy substance is observed in the bottom as well as a yellow film on top and a sour smell. This container is on a shelf next to cleaned dishes. The PIC was consulted and the container discarded during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. 

A potted plant is observed on the top shelf over the pizza prep station. This is not a good location for dirt/plants to be as there is a chance that it will contaminate the prep surfaces underneath or possible the foods when the lids are open. The PIC was consulted and the plant removed to correct.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. 

Multiple moist wiping cloths are observed on the counters throughout the food preparation areas. Education was conducted. These items should be held between uses in sanitizer solution. The cloths were moved during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-202.11: (A) Multiuse FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be smooth, free of breaks, cracks, sharp angles, and finished to have SMOOTH welds and joints. Also, it shall be accessible for cleaning and inspection with easy disassembling. 

A plastic tub is observed cracked and being held together with tape. This container was originally observed drying after washing with the tape still on. Tape is not a good material for repairs when moisture and/or food is involved. The PIC was consulted and instructed to replace the container if repairs are not able to produce a smooth and easily cleanable surface. The container was brought out of service during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur. 

An employee beverage was observed on a shelf int he back prep area next to food contact utensils and equipment. The item was shown to the PIC and moved to the area reserved for employee beverages during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
3-301.11: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall properly wash hands (C). (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall not contact RTE FOODS with bare hands  except washing fruits and veggies (P). (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize contact with FOOD that is not RTE (Pf). (D) Contact does not apply to RTE Food being added as ingredient to be cooked. (E) FOOD EMPLOYEES not serving a HSP may contact exposed, RTE with bare hands if approved. 

Observed food handling employee to be prepping salad topping materials. Employee was dicing washed tomatoes. Upon questioning, employee stated the diced tomatoes were for the tops of salads. No single-use gloves were being utilized. Cease practice. Ensure staff is aware that ready-to-eat (RTE) foods should be handled with single-use gloves after proper hand washing behaviors. Inspector asked employee to wash hands and don single-use gloves. COS. 

Observed one of the bar tenders to add a lemon to a drink without a single-use glove. Cease practice. Utilize tongs to add sliced fruits and/or single-use gloves. Sliced fruits are a RTE food and are being directly put into beverages. Ensure staff is aware to utilize single-use gloves when slicing fruits, as well. Discussed with bar tender. COS.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Observed the salad prep employee to be cutting washed whole tomatoes into a diced fashion; however, the washed tomatoes were placed back into the unwashed produce cardboard box. Cease practice. Ensure washed whole produce is not replaced back into the original cardboard container. Cardboard container is not a clean surface and can contribute to cross contamination after washing RTE food. Discussed with employee. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following food-contact surfaces in need of cleaning (wash, rinse, sanitize):
1. Both soda nozzle gun holders at the bar had a layer of mold. Inspector showed bartenders. Ensure the soda nozzles of the gun are cleaned as well a the holders were soda ponds and accumulations. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 11/2/22 and 4/4/23.
2. The inside and floors of the fryer area have a significant amount of food debris (several inches tall). The entire area of the fryers needs cleaned. All food debris needs to be removed. Debris is visible on the lines inside the fryers, lips, floor, etc. Layer of grease on the interior doors and inside of the fryers, as well as the floors.
3. The shelving of the walk-in cooler (not the meat/protein one) has a layer of food build-up and debris on the grating. Shelving needs power washed.

Discussed areas with PIC. Ensure staff is aware to clean these areas frequently in order to hinder an accumulation of debris, food splash, mold, etc. Inspector will follow-up on 9/18/23.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

(REPEAT) Observed multiple bottom prep coolers and the shelving units of the walk-in coolers to have rusted grating and paint is chipping off. Re-paint the shelving grates and/or re-seal and/or replace. Equipment should not be rusted and chipping inside food-contact areas - smooth, easily cleanable, corrosion resistant surfaces. Discussed with PIC. Correct by the next routine inspection. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 4/4/23.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following non-food contact areas in need of cleaning:
1. Prep line and cook line have some food debris and utensils under the line. Pull equipment as needed to clean and mop the floors. See #16 violation regarding the floors of the fryer area.
2. The shelving unit right next to the large stand mixer (across from the ice machine) has flour dust on the grates. Ensure to clean frequently to reduce flour dust on surfaces.
3. The spray nozzle of the 3 compartment sink has some mold on the underside of the sprayer. Ensure to clean routinely to prevent build-up.

Discussed routine cleaning of non-food contact surfaces with PIC. Ensure staff is aware to pay particular attention to the above areas. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following areas in need of repairs:
1. Coving around the dish machine area is coming away from the wall, as well as tiles being damaged or coming up off the flooring. Repeat since last routine inspection on 4/4/23.
2. Caulking/re-caulking is needed at: kitchen hand sink (missing - repeat since last routine inspection on 4/4/23), interior of the hand sinks (creases of metal) at the kitchen hand sink, dish machine hand sink, and bar hand sink need re-caulked (coming away).

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure the coving is re-put back on the wall (caulk to wall), tiles repaired and grouted to the floor, and caulking is completed before the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

(REPEAT) Observed the soda nozzles at the bar (multiple) to have mold accumulation, as well as all the soda nozzle holders at the bar. Ensure all soda nozzle gun covers are removed and washed, rinsed, and sanitized. Ensure no mold/mildew accumulation occurs in the soda nozzle holders - clean as needed to prevent build-up. Discussed with owner. Owner washed, rinsed, and sanitized the above areas. COS. Ensure staff is aware of routine cleaning in these areas. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 11/2/22.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

Observed multiple coolers to be missing thermometers. Ensure extra thermometers are purchased for the facility. Ensure all cold holding units have a thermometer within the inside. Discussed with head chef and owner. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

Multiple bottom prep coolers and reach-in coolers have shelving grates that are rusted and paint is chipping off of them. The walk-in cooler shelving units have similar issues. Re-paint the shelving grates and units and/or re-seal with sealant and/or replace. Equipment should not be rusted and chipping in food areas - smooth, easily cleanable, corrosion-resistant surfaces. Discussed with PIC. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.13: (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. (B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature. 

Observed no maximum registering thermometer and/or heat test strips for the facility. Discussed with PIC. Ensure facility has a method to measure the heat temperature of the dish machine in order to verify proper sanitizing levels of heat. Inspector will follow-up on 4/14/23.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following non-food contact areas in need of cleaning:
1. Several kitchen ceiling tiles and vents have dust.
2. Walk-in cooler has dusty fans.
3. Dry storage needs swept under shelving.
4. Several interior fryers were soiled with heavy food accumulation and grease. Flooring under the fryers is soiled with a layer of grease and grease debris.

Discussed routine cleaning of the above areas. Ensure staff is aware to clean. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. 

Observed the following areas in need of repairs:
1. Caulking/re-caulking needed at: kitchen hand sink (missing), prep tables and sink (caulking coming away from wall and equipment), 3 compartment sink and dish machine areas (moldy caulk - replace).
2. Coving around the dish machine area is coming away from the wall and/or has tiles missing.
3. Ceiling tile above heated dish machine is severely frayed and exposing the area above the ceiling tiles.

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure areas are re-caulked and/or caulked, coving is replaced and/or sealed, and the ceiling tile is replaced before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed no allergen training certifications for all certified food protection manager’s. Copies that were available were expired. Discussed with owner. Provided educational handout on how to acquire the training. Correct by next routine inspection. All CFPM’s should have additional allergen training certification. Print for office and/or upload onto the employee system.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

The inside of the ice machine has several locations with either black spots or pink slime observed. PIC instructed to ensure that the machine is cleaned often enough so as to protect the Ready-To-Eat foods (ice) within. The machine was cleaned during this inspection to correct the violation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple nozzles on the fountain drink machine are observed soiled and in need of cleaning. An employee was shown the items for verification and then moved all the nozzles to dish for washing.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
(REPEAT SITUATION) 4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination.

A butcher’s knife is observed stored between the wall and the knife rack next to the three part sink. This gap is not easily cleaned/sanitized and should not be a surface used for storing food contact items. The knife was moved during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

The shelves in both  of the walk in coolers are observed soiled and in need of cleaning. PIC instructed to clean and maintain  clean moving forward.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Several house flies are observed in the kitchen, specifically around the hand sink next to the dish area as well as the prep area in front of that sink. Amounts do not appear to have reduced from the previous follow-up, and so another follow up is being set for 2 weeks (after the fair). Cleaning and repair under the hand sink were discussed with the kitchen manger.  PIC thinks it is possible that a majority of the flies could be coming from the dumpster behind the facility. Cleaning is suggested. It is also suggested to contact pest control. Kitchen manager also discussed an air shield for the back door.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-301.11: (A) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be separated from one another for RETAIL sale. (B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be located in area not above FOOD or FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES. 

A can of Noble brand “Eliminate” spray (insecticide) is observed stored on a shelf next to metal quarter pans used for food prep/storage. This shelf is also over the three part sink that currently has cleaned strainers and silverware on it. PIC was consulted and the container moved during the inspection to correct the violation. PIC indicated that the current policy should have any of these types of chemicals stored in the office.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
